title: 4D530013-Blinx_The_Time_Sweeper.xiso.iso
replaces: tbflip424-blinx.json (46936c6a3d, registered, never measured: its Thor pilot was withdrawn under the owner's charging hold) and tbflip424-doa1u.json (231d04df51, Nova, stopped at its pilot review). The Thor is claiming requests again (titleroutes and lanelocal soaks ran on it 08:31Z to 13:46Z on 09-27), so the leg returns to the title the tracker row names. The legs below are tbflip424-blinx.json's, word for word in their thresholds; what changes is the ref, one M0 clause (m50) and the baseline. Nothing here is fitted to the DOA1U pilot: that pilot is a different title on a different device, and its two runs are reported in NOTES as they read.
why_a_new_ref: master now carries PR #465 (HAKUX_TCG68_JC on by default), so the binary the flip would ship in is not 46936c6a3d's. 00c2840810 is this branch's merge of origin/master f131dd11c6; the branch's own accel/ diff against master is empty (af6fffdc0c is the same change as #465's cf09ea47a1). Both arms run it, with JC on in both.

arms.A: 00c2840810, no --env: whole-page TB invalidation, the shipped default; HAKUX_TCG68_JC unset, so on
arms.B: 00c2840810, the same apk, --env HAKUX_TCG424_RANGE=1: range test plus per-page code bitmap. The env is the only independent variable.

runs: 4D530013-Blinx_The_Time_Sweeper.xiso.iso, --route survey, --seconds 540, --device thor, 3 runs per arm interleaved A B A B A B. Pilot = the first A and the first B (2 x (540 + 90) s = 21 min). 540 s because `mark play` falls ~257 s into the soak.
reader: python3 docs/lanes/tbflip424/playread.py <result ids>, at the commit that adds this file (it gains the m50 column; the window and every other column are unchanged from 442834864e). Window: `mark play` + 30 s to the end of the log. No mark = VOID. Per run: gfps = the median of the hakuX-perf gfps samples in the window; churn% = (jcus + rdus) / vCPU cpu over the [tlb68] lines in the window. Per arm: the median of its three per-run values. The survey route's span median is NOT read.
why_this_window: On Blinx the survey route is in the first stage before `mark play` (the START/A rounds pause and resume it). After the mark it only plays. Pass 1's frames show the stage under control from the first play frame on (0-0-y-1790433159-titleplay-p1-blinx/route-frames/110116-play.png onward). The 30 s settle is churn.py's own default.
why_this_title: The cost has to be able to show in gfps, so the vCPU thread has to be the busy one. In the window, vCPU cpu over wall (the [tlb68] cpu= and dt= fields, A-path runs on disk) reads 58-68% on Blinx on the Thor and 85-87% on Crimson, against 38-46% on DOA1 Ultimate. Blinx also churns little (rd% 1.9-2.6, jc% 0.2), so the range test has little to save there, and on tbchurn424's B runs it took 32-42k slow stores a second in this window against ~800-900 on A.
baseline_on_disk: playread.py, Thor, A path, all before #465 (JC off): pass 1 (a5b5b628f2, 420 s) gfps 15, churn% 2.3, ng 33, m50 8; tbchurn424 A (7e6a4ac88a, 300 s) gfps 12 / 11.0, churn% 2.2 / 2.8, ng 3 / 4, m50 6 / 21; tbchurn424 B (1d1251aa4b) gfps 10 / 13.5, churn% 0.0 / 0.0, m50 6 / 6. titlebench 2612887 (d0e30924f8, 420 s) is the Thor's slow state: gfps 2, ng 6, m50 1. JC's share of A's churn is 0.2 of 2.2-2.8, so A's churn with JC on is expected near 2.0-2.6.

legs.M0 (instrument): Every run has a `mark play` line, >= 20 gfps samples in the window, [tlb68] in >= 90% of the window's 2 s windows, xx = 0, and m50 >= 4 (at least four gfps samples >= 50 between `mark booted` and `mark play`: the title and menu screens run at the 59 cap on either arm, 6-21 such samples on the five normal runs on disk, B included, and 1 on the slow run). A's [tlb68] lines carry rt=0 only; B's carry rt=1 only. A run failing this is VOID, not zero: it is re-queued once on the same arm. More than one VOID run per arm stops the lane without a verdict. FAILS in a world where the route no longer reaches `mark play`, perf lines are missing, the Thor is in its slow state, or the env does not reach the emulator (B shows rt=0).
legs.M1 (the counter moves; the falsifier): Per-arm median churn%: A >= 1.0, and B <= 0.5 x A. Per-arm median di/s: B <= 0.1 x A. FAILS in a world where Blinx gameplay spends nothing on the two #424 mechanisms (A < 1.0: then the arm cannot show a cost that trades against a saving, and the M4' result is inert; report it and do not flip on it), or where the range test does not engage (B's churn stays near A's).
legs.M4' (must not regress, on gameplay): Per-arm median gfps: B >= A - 1. And no run of either arm crashes: no `Fatal signal` or `FATAL` line in logcat.txt, and the window's last gfps sample is within 15 s of the route's `soak end` line. FAILS in a world where the cost the range test adds on Blinx (32-42k invalidator entries a second, each answered under one page lock, where A takes ~500) outweighs the ~2% of the vCPU thread it saves. Then B's gameplay median falls by more than 1 gfps, which is ~8% at this title's 11-15 gfps.
legs.decision: Flip the default in hakux_tcg424_range_on() iff M0, M1 and M4' all pass. If M4' fails, do not flip: diagnose from fs/s, inv/s and slow/s, and report on #424. If M1 fails with A < 1.0, do not flip on this arm: report that Blinx gameplay cannot price the lever.

what_this_cannot_see: A regression smaller than the run-to-run spread. Three A-path medians on disk on the Thor read 11, 12 and 15, so a true loss under ~2 gfps can pass and a true zero can fail; M4' says which side of A - 1 three-run medians fell, and NOTES gives every run so the spread can be read beside it. Self-modifying code that a spared block should have caught; the range test makes invalidation do LESS. One title's first stage on one device. The pgraph must-not-move check on the flipped binary is a separate step, done after the flip.
expect_note: EMPTY ON PURPOSE: a soak writes no captures, so there is no golden key. The legs are read with playread.py off the [tlb68], hakuX-pages and hakuX-perf lines.
